title: 5 Day Kenya Bird Photography Safari
rank_math_title: Kenya Bird Photography Safari: 5 Wonderful Days in the Rift
rank_math_desc: Kenya bird photography safari for 5 days at Lakes Naivasha, Nakuru, Bogoria and Baringo: fish eagles, flamingos and hundreds of species. Price on request.
post_content: This Kenya bird photography safari follows the Rift Valley lakes, where fish eagles, flamingos and colourful bush birds give you a new subject every few minutes.
overview:
This Kenya bird photography safari is made for photographers who love birds. It visits four Rift Valley lakes in five days, each with different habitats and species, and the drives between them are short, so you spend more time shooting.

Kenya has well over 1,000 recorded bird species. The Rift Valley lakes hold a big share of them, from water birds and raptors to the bright little bush birds that make perfect close-ups.

Why choose this Kenya bird photography safari?

Bird photography needs patience and the right position. Your guide knows where the birds feed and roost, and the vehicle is private, so you can wait as long as you need for a bird to land or take off.

  • Lake Naivasha: boat rides close to African fish eagles as they swoop for fish.
  • Lake Nakuru: flamingos, pelicans and rhinos on the same shoreline.
  • Lake Bogoria: hot springs, geysers and, in good years, huge flocks of lesser flamingos.
  • Lake Baringo: a freshwater lake with herons, kingfishers and cliff-dwelling owls.

Birds you can photograph

Expect lilac-breasted rollers, superb starlings, kingfishers, hornbills, weavers and many raptors. Water birds include goliath herons, pelicans, cormorants and jacanas. At Baringo, local bird guides know the roosts of owls and nightjars.

Flamingo numbers move between lakes depending on water levels, so your guide will check the latest reports. Read our Lake Bogoria guide and Lake Nakuru safari guide for more on each lake.

Best time for a Kenya bird photography safari

Birding is good all year. From October to April, migrant birds from Europe and Asia join the resident species, and many birds wear breeding colours during the rains. The dry months from June to September give easier roads and clear light.

Gear for bird photography

  • A 150-600 mm or 200-500 mm lens is ideal. A teleconverter helps with small birds.
  • Use a high shutter speed (1/3200 s or more) for birds in flight.
  • Bean bags are provided in the vehicle. A small monopod is useful on the boats.

Prefer a classic birding trip without the photography focus? See our 5 day Kenya birding safari or all birding safaris. For background reading, the Nature Kenya website has helpful notes on Kenya's birds.

faq.a: Most guests see between 200 and 300 species in five days, depending on the season. Your guide keeps a list for you.

faq.q: What lens do I need for the Kenya bird photography safari?
faq.a: A 150-600 mm or 200-500 mm zoom works best. Bring a teleconverter for small birds and a shorter zoom for flocks and landscapes.
Yes. The boat rides on Lake Naivasha and Lake Baringo are included, along with the park fees for Lake Nakuru and Lake Bogoria.

faq.a: October to April brings migrant birds and breeding colours. June to September is drier, with easier roads. Birding is rewarding all year.

itinerary.label: Day 1
itinerary.title: Nairobi to Lake Naivasha
itinerary.content: Drive from Nairobi into the Rift Valley, stopping at the viewpoint on the escarpment. After lunch at your lodge, take a boat ride on Lake Naivasha to photograph African fish eagles diving for fish, plus hippos, kingfishers and herons along the papyrus.

itinerary.label: Day 2
itinerary.title: Lake Naivasha to Lake Nakuru
itinerary.content: A short morning drive to Lake Nakuru National Park. Spend the day on the shoreline and in the acacia woodland, photographing flamingos, pelicans and storks, as well as rhinos, buffaloes and Rothschild's giraffes.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.title: Lake Nakuru to Lake Bogoria and Lake Baringo
itinerary.content: Drive north to Lake Bogoria, where steam rises from hot springs and flamingos feed on the soda water. Continue to Lake Baringo in the afternoon for your first birding walk around the lodge grounds.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.title: Lake Baringo boat ride and cliff walk
itinerary.content: Start with an early boat ride for herons, kingfishers, jacanas and fish eagles. Later, walk with a local bird guide to the cliffs and acacia scrub to look for owls, hornbills and colourful bush birds. Evening in the hide or around the lodge.

itinerary.label: Day 5
itinerary.title: Lake Baringo to Nairobi
itinerary.content: One more early morning of birding by the lake, then breakfast and the drive back to Nairobi, arriving in the late afternoon.
